The test image shows a tomato plant laid flat, displaying the stem and root system. Key features:
- Bleached/pale whitish-tan stems with brown lesions
- Severe wilting and plant collapse
- Stem girdling near the soil line
- Brown/rotted roots
- Dead brown leaves

This looks like a stem/root disease with stem girdling. Let me check the part index and then reference images.

The plant part is stem/whole plant (pulled up, showing stem girdling at soil line). Top candidates from stem section: **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**, **Southern_Blight**, **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**, **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**.

Now viewing one reference from each of 4 top candidates:

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image** (Bugwood ID 1568040): Tomato plant pulled from ground, showing bleached/pale stems, brown root rot, full plant collapse and wilting.
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** reference: Bleached stem with embedded black sclerotia — test image lacks visible sclerotia.
- **Southern_Blight** reference: Shows bleached inner stem tissue with water-soaked outer lesion — no white cottony mycelium mat visible in test image.
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt** reference (Bugwood ID 1568041): Consecutive ID to the test image (1568040), strongly suggesting same disease series. Shows brown internal pith discoloration — matches the vascular/pith rot pattern in the test image.
- **Alternaria** reference: Microscopic spores — no match.

The consecutive Bugwood IDs, combined with the whole-plant wilt with bleached/pale stems and brown root/vascular discoloration, points clearly to **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**.
